entities.summary:
Barak Khan (barak-khan): A prominent economist and social scientist of the Classical era, active in the Golden Horde, was known for his work on monarchs and rulers. He contributed significantly to the understanding of the region's political dynamics and social structures.

    Born in an unknown year, Barak Khan lived until 1428, leaving a lasting legacy in the field of social science. His work continues to influence contemporary scholars and researchers.

    Barak Khan's contributions to the field of monarchs and rulers had a profound impact on the understanding of the Golden Horde's political landscape, shaping the way historians and researchers approach the subject today.

    The study of Barak Khan's work has also shed light on the complex relationships between the Golden Horde's leaders and the social structures of the time, providing valuable insights into the lives of the people living in the region during the Classical era.
